title: High-dose carboplatin + etoposide with stem-cell rescue
context_label: Relapsed germ-cell cancer · specialist transplant pathway
indication_text: Metastatic relapsed/refractory germ-cell tumours. Specialist autologous conditioning pathway.
purpose: Aim for lasting cancer control or cure in selected relapsed germ-cell cancer, using high-dose chemotherapy with your own stored stem cells.
schedule_label: Chemotherapy days −5 to −3 · stem cells day 0

agents.name: Carboplatin
agents.explanation: Carboplatin is a platinum-containing chemotherapy. Inside cells, it forms chemical attachments to DNA, including links that stop DNA strands working normally. This disrupts copying and repair and can lead to cell death. Healthy cells can also be injured, especially blood-forming cells in the bone marrow. The kidneys help remove carboplatin, so kidney function is used to calculate the dose. AUC 5 describes a target drug exposure over time; it is not a fixed dose of 5 mg.
agents.watch: Low blood counts, nausea and vomiting can occur. An allergic reaction is also possible: tell the nurse immediately if you feel flushed, itchy, tight-chested or unwell during the drip.
risks: Low blood counts, infection or bleeding

agents.name: Etoposide
agents.explanation: Etoposide interferes with an enzyme used to copy and repair DNA. This can stop cancer cells growing and can also lower healthy blood counts.
agents.watch: Report fever, bleeding, a sore mouth or feeling faint during an infusion.
risks: Low blood counts and serious infection
Infusion reaction or low blood pressure

anatomy: Report ringing ears, hearing changes, confusion or new weakness.
Mouth ulcers may make eating and drinking difficult; ask for pain and nutrition support.

Report vomiting, diarrhoea, severe pain or inability to drink.
Profound low counts are expected. Fever or sudden illness needs immediate treatment.

rows.label: Medicines and practical care
cells: Confirm admission, stored stem-cell availability, fertility discussion and the complete transplant-support prescription before conditioning.

Chemotherapy and stem-cell rescue take place in a specialist transplant service. Carboplatin runs over 30 minutes and etoposide over two hours on each treatment day. Preparation, fluid management and monitoring add time. Staff give stem-cell infusion premedication under the local plan.

Prescribed anti-sickness treatment is needed across the high-dose days. The local transplant plan includes antiviral and antifungal prevention, mouth care, a proton-pump inhibitor and Pneumocystis pneumonia prevention. Co-trimoxazole starts only after engraftment; the team specifies the stop date. Irradiated cellular blood components are required from one week before conditioning until 12 months after stem-cell infusion.
Review lasting effects, support needs and any line/pump removal.

rows.label: Cancer treatment and follow-up
cells: Relapsed germ-cell cancer · specialist transplant pathway

Your stem cells help restore blood-cell production after intensive chemotherapy; they are not donor cells. A second high-dose course may be considered after recovery, at least 28 days later, depending on response and toxicity. Later oral etoposide is only considered in selected responders after two courses and is not automatic.
Your consultant sets scan and response-review timing for your cancer and treatment intent. Safety blood tests do not by themselves show whether treatment is working.
Agree oncology/urology follow-up and the next treatment or surveillance plan.

evidence.title: High-dose chemotherapy and stem-cell rescue · Einhorn 2007
evidence.summary: In a retrospective series of 184 previously treated patients, 116 remained in complete remission without relapse during a median follow-up of 48 months. Three treatment-related deaths and three later cases of acute leukaemia were reported.
evidence.intro: In a retrospective series of 184 previously treated patients, 116 remained in complete remission without relapse during a median follow-up of 48 months. Three treatment-related deaths and three later cases of acute leukaemia were reported.
evidence.caveat: This was not a randomised comparison. It used carboplatin 700 mg/m², whereas NCCP 00453 uses AUC7. The study supports the treatment approach but its dose and outcomes must not be presented as identical to this protocol.
evidence.interpretation: This was not a randomised comparison. It used carboplatin 700 mg/m², whereas NCCP 00453 uses AUC7. The study supports the treatment approach but its dose and outcomes must not be presented as identical to this protocol.

questions.q: What is the treatment trying to do?
questions.a: Aim for lasting cancer control or cure in selected relapsed germ-cell cancer, using high-dose chemotherapy with your own stored stem cells. Your stem cells help restore blood-cell production after intensive chemotherapy; they are not donor cells. A second high-dose course may be considered after recovery, at least 28 days later, depending on response and toxicity. Later oral etoposide is only considered in selected responders after two courses and is not automatic.

Carboplatin AUC7 is followed by etoposide 750 mg/m² on days −5, −4 and −3. Your stored stem cells are infused on day 0. Growth-factor injections start on day +1 and continue until the team confirms neutrophil recovery. These day numbers are relative to the stem-cell infusion.

questions.q: Does a delay mean treatment has failed?
questions.a: No. Blood counts, organ function and symptoms can make a delay or dose change safer. Your team decides whether and when to give the next dose.

questions.q: Who do I contact if unwell?
questions.a: Use your verified oncology daytime or out-of-hours number. If you cannot reach the team, seek urgent medical assessment. Severe symptoms require 112/999.
